Appendix A: Summary of guidelines

Rule 1.1 Mandatory
The program shall not violate the standard C syntax and constraints, nor exceed the implementation's translation limits.

Rule 1.2 Mandatory
Language extensions shall not be used.

Rule 1.3 Mandatory
Undefined and critical unspecified behaviour shall not occur.

Rule 2.1 Mandatory
A project shall not contain unreachable code.

Rule 2.2 Mandatory
There shall be no dead code.

Rule 2.3 Advisory
A project should not contain unused type declarations

Rule 2.4 Advisory
A project should not contain unused tag declarations

Rule 2.5 Advisory
A project should not contain unused macro declarations

Rule 2.6 Advisory
A function should not contain unused label declarations

Rule 2.7 Advisory
There should be no unused parameters in functions

Rule 3.1 Mandatory
The character sequences `/*` and `//` shall not be used within a comment

Rule 3.2 Mandatory
Line-splicing shall not be used in `//` comments

Rule 4.1 Mandatory
Octal and hexadecimal escape sequences shall be terminated

Rule 4.2 Advisory
Trigraphs should not be used

Rule 5.1 Mandatory
External identifiers shall be distinct

Rule 5.2 Mandatory
Identifiers declared in the same scope and name space shall be distinct

Rule 5.3 Mandatory
An identifier declared in an inner scope shall not hide an identifier declared in an outer scope

Rule 5.4 Mandatory
Macro identifiers shall be distinct

Rule 5.5 Mandatory
Identifiers shall be distinct from macro names

Rule 5.6 Mandatory
A typedef name shall be a unique identifier

Rule 5.7 Mandatory
A tag name shall be a unique identifier

Rule 5.8 Mandatory
Identifiers that define objects or functions with external linkage shall be unique

Rule 5.9 Advisory
Identifiers that define objects or functions with internal linkage should be unique

Rule 6.1 Mandatory
Bit-fields shall only be declared with an appropriate type

Rule 6.2 Mandatory
Single-bit named bit fields shall not be of a signed type

Rule 7.1 Mandatory
Octal constants shall not be used

Rule 7.2 Mandatory
A "u" or "U" suffix shall be applied to all integer constants that are represented in an unsigned type

Rule 7.3 Mandatory
The lowercase character 'l' shall not be used in a literal suffix

Rule 7.4 Mandatory
A string literal shall not be assigned to an object unless the object's type is “pointer to const-qualified char”

Rule 8.1 Mandatory
Types shall be explicitly specified

Rule 8.2 Mandatory
Function types shall be in prototype form with named parameters

Rule 8.3 Mandatory
All declarations of an object or function shall use the same names and type qualifiers

Rule 8.4 Mandatory
A compatible declaration shall be visible when an object or function with external linkage is defined

Rule 8.5 Mandatory
An external object or function shall be declared once in one and only one file

Rule 8.6 Mandatory
An identifier with external linkage shall have exactly one external definition

Rule 8.7 Advisory
Functions and objects should not be defined with external linkage if they are referenced in only one translation unit

Rule 8.8 Mandatory
The static storage class specifier shall be used in all declarations of objects and functions that have internal linkage

Rule 8.9 Advisory
An object should be defined at block scope if its identifier only appears in a single function

Rule 8.10 Mandatory
An inline function shall be declared with the static storage class

Rule 8.11 Advisory
When an array with external linkage is declared, its size should be explicitly specified

Rule 8.12 Mandatory
Within an enumerator list, the value of an implicitly specified enumeration constant shall be unique

Rule 8.13 Advisory
A pointer should point to a const-qualified type whenever possible

Rule 8.14 Mandatory
The restrict type qualifier shall not be used

Rule 9.1 Mandatory
The value of an object with automatic storage duration shall not be read before it has been set

Rule 9.2 Mandatory
The initializer for an aggregate or union shall be enclosed in braces

Rule 9.3 Mandatory
Arrays shall not be partially initialized

Rule 9.4 Mandatory
An element of an object shall not be initialised more than once

Rule 9.5 Mandatory
Where designated initialisers are used to initialize an array object the size of the array shall be specified explicitly

Rule 10.1 Mandatory
Operands shall not be of an inappropriate essential type

Rule 10.2 Advisory
Expressions of essentially character type shall not be used inappropriately in addition and subtraction operations

Rule 10.3 Mandatory
The value of an expression shall not be assigned to an object with a narrower essential type or of a different essential type category

Rule 10.4 Mandatory
Both operands of an operator in which the usual arithmetic conversions are performed shall have the same essential type category

Rule 10.5 Advisory
The value of an expression should not be cast to an inappropriate essential type

Rule 10.6 Mandatory
The value of a composite expression shall not be assigned to an object with wider essential type

Rule 10.7 Mandatory
If a composite expression is used as one operand of an operator in which the usual arithmetic conversions are performed then the other operand shall not have wider essential type

Rule 10.8 Mandatory
The value of a composite expression shall not be cast to a different essential type category or a wider essential type

Rule 11.1 Mandatory
Conversions shall not be performed between a pointer to a function and any other type

Rule 11.2 Mandatory
Conversions shall not be performed between a pointer to incomplete and any other type

Rule 11.3 Mandatory
A cast shall not be performed between a pointer to object type and a pointer to a different object type

Rule 11.4 Advisory
A conversion should not be performed between a pointer to object and an integer type

Rule 11.5 Advisory
A conversion should not be performed from pointer to void into pointer to object

Rule 11.6 Mandatory
A cast shall not be performed between pointer to void and an arithmetic type

Rule 11.7 Mandatory
A cast shall not be performed between pointer to object and a non-integer arithmetic type

Rule 11.8 Mandatory
A cast shall not remove any const or volatile qualification from the type pointed to by a pointer

Rule 11.9 Mandatory
The macro NULL shall be the only permitted form of integer null pointer constant

Rule 12.1 Advisory
The precedence of operators within expressions should be made explicit

Rule 12.2 Mandatory
The right hand operand of a shift operator shall lie in the range zero to one less than the width in bits of the essential type of the left hand operand

Rule 12.3 Advisory
The comma operator should not be used

Rule 12.4 Advisory
Evaluation of constant expressions should not lead to unsigned integer wrap-around

Rule 13.1 Mandatory
Initialiser lists shall not contain persistent side effects

Rule 13.2 Mandatory
The value of an expression and its persistent side effects shall be the same under all permitted evaluation orders

Rule 13.3 Advisory
A full expression containing an increment (++) or decrement (--) operator should have no other potential side effects other than that caused by the increment or decrement operator

Rule 13.4 Advisory
The result of an assignment operator should not be used

Rule 13.5 Mandatory
The right hand operand of a logical && or || operator shall not contain persistent side effects

Rule 13.6 Mandatory
The operand of the sizeof operator shall not contain any expression which has potential side effects

Rule 14.1 Advisory
A loop counter shall not have essentially floating type

Rule 14.2 Mandatory
A for loop shall be well-formed

Rule 14.3 Mandatory
Controlling expressions shall not be invariant

Rule 14.4 Mandatory
The controlling expression of an if statement and the controlling expression of an iteration-statement shall have essentially Boolean type

Rule 15.1 Advisory
The goto statement should not be used

Rule 15.2 Mandatory
The goto statement shall jump to a label declared later in the same function

Rule 15.3 Mandatory
Any label referenced by a goto statement shall be declared in the same block, or in any block enclosing the goto statement

Rule 15.4 Advisory
There should be no more than one break or goto statement used to terminate any iteration statement

Rule 15.5 Advisory
A function should have a single point of exit at the end

Rule 15.6 Mandatory
The body of an iteration-statement or a selection-statement shall be a compound statement

Rule 15.7 Mandatory
All if . . else if constructs shall be terminated with an else statement

Rule 16.1 Mandatory
All switch statements shall be well-formed

Rule 16.2 Mandatory
A switch label shall only be used when the most closely-enclosing compound statement is the body of a switch statement

Rule 16.3 Mandatory
An unconditional break statement shall terminate every switch-clause

Rule 16.4 Mandatory
Every switch statement shall have a default label

Rule 16.5 Mandatory
A default label shall appear as either the first or the last switch label of a switch statement

Rule 16.6 Mandatory
Every switch statement shall have at least two switch-clauses

Rule 16.7 Mandatory
A switch-expression shall not have essentially Boolean type

Rule 17.1 Mandatory
The features of `<stdarg.h>` shall not be used

Rule 17.2 Mandatory
Functions shall not call themselves, either directly or indirectly

Rule 17.3 Mandatory
A function shall not be declared implicitly

Rule 17.4 Mandatory
All exit paths from a function with non-void return type shall have an explicit return statement with an expression

Rule 17.5 Advisory
The function argument corresponding to a parameter declared to have an array type shall have an appropriate number of elements

Rule 17.6 Mandatory
The declaration of an array parameter shall not contain the static keyword between the `[ ]`

Rule 17.7 Mandatory
The value returned by a function having non-void return type shall be used

Rule 17.8 Advisory
A function parameter should not be modified

Rule 18.1 Mandatory
A pointer resulting from arithmetic on a pointer operand shall address an element of the same array as that pointer operand

Rule 18.2 Mandatory
Subtraction between pointers shall only be applied to pointers that address elements of the same array

Rule 18.3 Mandatory
The relational operators >, >=, < and <= shall not be applied to objects of pointer type except where they point into the same object

Rule 18.4 Advisory
The +, -, += and -= operators should not be applied to an expression of pointer type

Rule 18.5 Advisory
Declarations should contain no more than two levels of pointer nesting

Rule 18.6 Mandatory
The address of an object with automatic storage shall not be copied to another object that persists after the first object has ceased to exist

Rule 18.7 Mandatory
Flexible array members shall not be declared

Rule 18.8 Mandatory
Variable-length array types shall not be used

Rule 19.1 Mandatory
An object shall not be assigned or copied to an overlapping object

Rule 19.2 Advisory
The union keyword should not be used

Rule 20.1 Mandatory
All #include directives shall precede any other content in the translation unit.

Rule 20.3 Mandatory
The #include directive shall be followed by either a `<filename>` or "filename" sequence

Rule 20.4 Mandatory
A macro shall not be defined with the same name as a keyword

Rule 20.5 Advisory
#undef should not be used

Rule 20.6 Mandatory
Tokens that look like a preprocessing directive shall not occur within a macro argument

Rule 20.7 Mandatory
Expressions resulting from the expansion of macro parameters shall be enclosed in parentheses

Rule 20.8 Mandatory
The controlling expression of a #if or #elif preprocessing directive shall evaluate to 0 or 1

Rule 20.9 Mandatory
The controlling expression of a #if or #elif directive shall only contain identifiers that are defined macros or C keywords.

Rule 20.10 Mandatory
The # operator shall not be used.

Rule 20.11 Mandatory
A macro parameter shall not be used with both the # and ## operators.

Rule 20.12 Mandatory
The ## operator shall not be used with a macro parameter that is also used in another macro invocation.

Rule 20.13 Mandatory
Preprocessor directives that are not defined shall not be used.

Rule 20.14 Mandatory
All #if, #ifdef and #ifndef directives shall have a matching #endif directive in the same file.

Rule 21.1 Mandatory
Reserved identifiers, keywords and macro names shall not be used.

Rule 21.2 Mandatory
A reserved identifier shall not be declared or defined.

Rule 21.3 Mandatory
The memory allocation and deallocation functions of <stdlib.h> shall not be used.

Rule 21.4 Mandatory
The <setjmp.h> header shall not be included.

Rule 21.5 Mandatory
The <signal.h> header shall not be included.

Rule 21.6 Mandatory
The standard library input/output functions shall not be used.

Rule 21.7 Mandatory
The atof, atoi, atol and atoll functions of <stdlib.h> shall not be used.

Rule 21.8 Mandatory
The abort, exit and getenv functions of <stdlib.h> shall not be used.

Rule 21.9 Mandatory
The bsearch and qsort functions of <stdlib.h> shall not be used.

Rule 21.10 Mandatory
The <time.h> header shall not be included.

Rule 21.11 Mandatory
The <tgmath.h> header shall not be included.

Rule 21.12 Mandatory
The fenv facilities of <fenv.h> shall not be used.
